data.name: Immortal Empire
data.detailed_description:
See other games by Tactic Studios


Acerca do jogo

Immortal Empire is a multiplayer tactics role playing game. Control a party of up to 5 immortals as you travel through a unique fantasy world, using spells and strategy to defeat your enemies.

Features
  • Play co-op with your friends, or destroy them in versus mode.
  • Unravel a mysterious storyline complete with fully voiced characters in the campaign.
  • Use automated matchmaking to compete in the PvP ladder.
  • Participate in official tournaments and win rewards.
  • Choose between 13 unique immortals, level up, collect loot, enchant your gear to fully customise your party.
  • Your dialog choices matter, the way you behave may form relationships or grant powerful character attibutes.
  • Try the challenging co-op Gauntlet mode where you must work together with other players to defeat enemy waves of increasing difficulty.
  • Use strategy and synergize spells to defeat challenging bosses.

Control a party of up to 5 immortals as you travel through a unique fantasy world, using spells and strategy to defeat your enemies. Play co-op, versus, or solo through a compelling campaign storyline with fully voiced characters.

reviews.review:
Immortal Empire is a tactical role-playing game that combines turn-based battles, character development, party building, and multiplayer elements within a fantasy setting. Developed and published by Tactic Studios Inc., it revolves around assembling a group of powerful immortals and learning how their individual abilities work together. Instead of emphasizing fast action, the game rewards planning, positioning, effective use of skills, and careful preparation before difficult encounters. Its mixture of campaign progression and multiplayer-oriented features gives it more variety than its relatively modest presentation might initially suggest.

The combat system is the heart of the experience. Players can command a party containing as many as five immortals, with each character offering different abilities and tactical possibilities. Selecting characters is therefore about more than choosing whoever appears strongest. A well-designed party needs abilities that complement one another, particularly when dealing with challenging enemy formations and stronger opponents. Positioning also matters because effective placement can determine whether an ability reaches the right target or whether a vulnerable character becomes exposed. Battles gradually encourage more deliberate decision-making as the player becomes familiar with each immortal.

There are 13 immortals available, creating considerable room for experimentation. Players can develop favorites, construct specialized parties, or change their lineup when a particular encounter demands a different approach. Character progression reinforces this flexibility through leveling and equipment. Weapons, armor, and other useful items can be collected, while an enchantment system provides additional opportunities to improve equipment. These mechanics give players several ways to strengthen their forces beyond simply gaining levels, making the preparation between battles almost as important as the decisions made during combat.

The campaign provides a structured introduction to the world and its characters while gradually revealing the mystery surrounding the Empire. Fully voiced characters add personality to the adventure and help distinguish the different immortals beyond their combat statistics. Conversations can also have gameplay consequences, as certain dialogue choices may influence relationships or grant attributes. It is a welcome feature because it gives the narrative portions some relevance to character development rather than treating conversations entirely as pauses between tactical encounters.

Multiplayer was designed as another major component of the experience. Cooperative gameplay allows players to combine their forces, while competitive battles provide an opportunity to test character combinations and tactical knowledge against human opponents. The PvP ladder and matchmaking systems add structure to competitive play. There is also the Gauntlet, a cooperative challenge involving progressively tougher waves of enemies. This mode suits the game's mechanics particularly well because surviving increasingly dangerous opposition requires efficient character combinations and good ability management.

The multiplayer focus does create one of the game's most significant concerns for present-day players. Features such as matchmaking, competitive ladders, cooperative sessions, and tournaments naturally become less appealing when an older game's active population declines. Someone primarily interested in solo tactical RPG gameplay can still find enjoyment in the campaign and progression systems, but players considering it mainly for competitive multiplayer should recognize that their experience can depend heavily on finding other active participants.

Its free-to-play model makes the game easy to sample without an upfront purchase. Gameplay rewards an in-game currency known as Radiance, which can contribute toward unlocking immortals and obtaining useful progression resources. Optional purchases exist for players who want them, but the basic structure still provides opportunities to progress through ordinary play. The progression loop of completing encounters, gaining resources, improving equipment, and experimenting with different immortals can become quite engaging for players who enjoy optimizing RPG parties.

Presentation is more functional than spectacular. The fantasy environments, character designs, effects, and interface communicate the necessary information, but the game inevitably shows its age when compared with newer tactical RPGs. Animations and environmental detail are relatively modest, and newcomers accustomed to highly polished modern productions may need time to adjust. Fortunately, the underlying strategic mechanics carry more weight than the visual spectacle. Once battles become more demanding, thinking about ability combinations and party composition becomes considerably more important than graphical complexity.

Steam Deck compatibility is less straightforward. Immortal Empire does not have a prominent official Steam Deck Verified or Playable classification to rely upon, so it should be treated as an unverified experience rather than a game specifically optimized for Valve's handheld. Because it was designed around traditional PC controls and an older interface, players may encounter control or usability issues and could need custom controller mappings, trackpad input, or other adjustments. Anyone purchasing or installing it specifically for Steam Deck should therefore expect possible configuration work rather than assuming seamless handheld operation.

Overall, Immortal Empire is a surprisingly layered tactical RPG whose strongest qualities come from combining party composition, turn-based combat, equipment progression, character abilities, and cooperative or competitive systems. The ability to build a five-character team from a larger selection of immortals encourages experimentation, while equipment and enchanting provide additional reasons to continue developing a preferred lineup. Its aging presentation and dependence on multiplayer activity prevent every aspect from retaining its original appeal, but its tactical foundations remain interesting for players who enjoy methodical fantasy RPG combat. It is best approached today as a niche strategy RPG with worthwhile character-building mechanics rather than primarily as a thriving competitive multiplayer experience.

Rating: 7/10
